resources.title: Study pack: Building a post-quantum CA with MTCs
Building a post-quantum certificate authority with Merkle Tree Certificates
Merkle Tree Certificates in plain words

learning.goal: Understand both the post-quantum scaling problem that pushes the Web PKI to change and, step by step, how Merkle Tree Certificates are issued and verified and why they save space.
gaps: hash functions (basis for Merkle trees and inclusion proofs)
digital signatures and public/private keys (basis for certificates, checkpoints, cosignatures)
certificate chains and X.509 (builds on digital signatures; needed for 'certificate chains', 'intermediate elision')
root programs / root stores (builds on certificate chains; needed for Chrome's Quantum-resistant Root Store)
why quantum computers threaten today's signatures (builds on digital signatures)
post-quantum signature and key sizes (builds on the quantum threat; the core of the scaling problem)
certificate transparency logs and monitors (builds on certificates and CAs)
Merkle trees (builds on hash functions; core of MTCs)
inclusion and consistency proofs (builds on Merkle trees)
checkpoints (signed tree heads) and cosigners/mirrors (builds on digital signatures and consistency proofs)
ACME (builds on certificates and domain validation)
downgrade attacks (builds on PQ vs classical authentication; needed for CT monitoring of PQ downgrades)
